A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VeilGen/DeVeiler research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original restoration experiments on SL and MRL optical systems, quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–2, component ablations in Tables 3–5, and a supplementary data-efficiency study.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds optical simulation results, a physical glare measurement, and resolution-chart and HDR restoration examples in Figures 10 and 13.

M1.justification: The three-stage VeilGen–DDN–DeVeiler pipeline, LOTGMP/VGIM/VGCM components, Algorithm 1 and training objectives remain unchanged. Added descriptions of the prediction heads document implementation details without establishing an architectural or procedural change.

E1.justification: The training datasets, two optical systems and principal Source, Screen-Compound and Realworld-Compound domains remain. V2 adds targeted black-screen glare-isolation and ISO resolution-chart scenarios, alongside an explicitly identified HDR stress example in Figure 13.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same single-degradation, cascaded and domain-adaptation comparators. Table 4 still compares CycleGAN, Degradation Transfer, HazeGen and VeilGen. The added diagnostics do not introduce or remove competing methods.

E3.justification: The new black-screen diagnostic uses approximately zero scene signal with side illumination to isolate glare (Section 11). Figure 10 adds simulated RMS spot evaluation at three viewing angles per lens. Existing benchmark splits, restoration metrics, preprocessing and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a physical interpretability check comparing a measured glare distribution with the predicted map, plus ISO-chart and HDR robustness case studies (Figure 13). Figure 10 adds optical spot analysis across viewing angles. Existing component ablations and the data-efficiency study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars for the experiments. The retained data-efficiency curve still presents point values; Table 1's percentages remain improvement rates, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Scores in Tables 1–5 and the retained data-efficiency curve are unchanged. V2 adds simulated spot measurements, including on-axis RMS values of 85.68 micrometers for SL and 2.55 micrometers for MRL (Figure 10), and qualitative findings on glare-map agreement, line-detail recovery and HDR restoration (Section 11/Figure 13).

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the diffusion sampling formulation and the supplementary affine-alignment equations are retained. Expanded explanations of multiplicative transmission and additive glare restate the existing model; no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same generation, reversible-restoration and superior-performance claims. V2 foregrounds glare-specific novelty in the introduction, but this focus was already explained in v1 Appendix B. The terminology changes do not establish a different substantive contribution.

C2.justification: New Section 8 explains practical generalization through lens-specific adaptation, alternative source-data acquisition and limited target data. Section 11 interprets measured glare agreement as physical validation. The introduction revises the hardware-suppression rationale. Existing limitations concerning saturation, fixed scene depth and implicit light representations remain.

D1.justification: Figure 10 newly documents field of view, f-number, total optical length and optical layouts for both systems. Section 9 explicitly identifies the transmission/glare heads as convolutional layers. Training schedules, hardware and the promise of future code/data release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 removes the super-resolution paper incorrectly cited for image decomposition in v1 and points that discussion to the already included Single image veiling glare removal paper. Section 8 adds limited positioning relative to prior lens-specific retraining practices, using existing references.

P1.justification: Targeted edits condense introduction and related-work passages, replace 'compact' with 'simplified' in central descriptions, and expand explanations. V2 adds Generalization Analysis and an acknowledgment, and renumbers supplementary sections from A–E to 6–11. The overall narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: V2 adds the optical-layout/spot-diagram Figure 10 and diagnostic Figure 13. Existing figures remain with supplementary relocation and renumbering, corrected panel labels in Figures 8–9, and an expanded Figure 2 caption. Benchmark table structures and existing visual comparisons are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves technical transparency through optical specifications and head-implementation details, and supplements v1's internal-feature evidence with a physical glare measurement and targeted restoration examples. These provide modest additional support and clarity. The new diagnostics remain qualitative, and the generalization discussion largely reuses existing experiments; the core method and benchmark conclusions are unchanged.
